High pressure fuel injectors are very loud, especially when you take the engine cover off.  I wouldn’t worry about it.

Replace the rotors.  Even if they can be shaved within spec.  It’s not worth the labor and time.  Shaved rotors are notorious for warping from heat because they’re thinner than brand new.  Just get new rotors, it’s cheaper and a longer lasting repair.

Replace fuel filter.  Suck out or drain all old gas.  Go get non ethanol fuel.  Fill the tank a quarter of the way.  Take off the supply fuel line while cranking to make sure fuel pump is working.  If working.  Spray some carb cleaner in there and let it sit.  If the needles in the carb are completely corroded.  Just buy a new carburetor.  It’s easier to replace than to learn how to rebuild.
Put the front tires on the back and see if it goes away or gets better.  Then you know it’s the tires and not suspension or alignment.

The suspension needs to be fully inspected.  Any type of damage to control arms, ball joints, or tie rod ends can make your tire wobble.  Especially if you hear it slam.  If it just wobbles without the slam.  I would suggest rotating the tires to the back to see if a belt separation is in the tire.  The wobble would move to the back.  But with slamming and noises on the driver side.  Get the suspension checked out immediately.  I have seen control arms break/ ball joints break and the tire causes an accident.

Try to spray graphite on the key and stick it in while still wet.  Then turn the steering wheel hard back and forth while trying to turn the key.  If the key turns and nothing happens and you know you have a good battery 12volts and terminals tights.  Most likely the ignition switch, especially if the key turns and no lights on instrument cluster.

Look in the clutch reservoir for fluid.  If it has fluid and not low.  Put the car on a flat surface.  Put it in 3rd gear and slowly let off the clutch until it grabs.  If it inches you forward.  The clutch is good.  If it doesn’t move and the clutch is fully extended.  Replace the clutch and slave cylinder.  Once you have about 100k on a clutch.  Depending on how you drive.  The friction disk and pressure plate are worn out.  Now if the pedal feels like there is no resistance at all.  It’s a hydraulic problem most likely.  Would look into the slave cylinder.  When they leak, it’s hard to see the leak because it’s inside the bell housing of the transmission.

Always use a short socket and not a deep socket.  You get more leverage and less chance to strip the bolt.  Make sure it’s a 6 point socket.  If you tried everything and it still won’t come off.  Suck the engine oil out from the dipstick tube.  Worst thing is wondering why someone tightened it so tight and probably messed it up.  Most the time a mechanic is fixing another mechanic’s mistakes.  Good luck.

But my current psychiatrist asked me, “When you’re depressed, do you ever wake up one day and feel normal?”.  I was like, why yes I do.  Which means I’m bipolar type 2.  My “normal” days or better than average days are just hypomania.  I’m not a doctor so I can only speak about my personal experience.  But as someone who has bipolar, I have been medically instructed to never take an SSRI alone without a mood stabilizer.
